clue.text: Couple got together over on island

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: I is the usual abbreviation for island on maps

indicators.note: over signals that the word for got together is turned backwards

parts.note: people who got together met

explanation.surface: A pair of lovers have been reunited on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a verb meaning join, but it is a noun: a romantic pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantically linked pair are informally called an item, as in gossip columns.

clue.text: Travel document one's left as train's moving across station

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stretch across the station, sitting either side of it
moving tells us the letters of as and train's are set in motion into a new order
one's left, read as one is left out, removes the numeral from the word train's

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
ITV1 is a British television channel, its 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A traveller worries about paperwork while a train pulls through a station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' drops I from TRAINS; 'moving' scrambles AS and TRANS into TRANS...SA, and 'across' places ITV1 in the middle. ITV1 is a British TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit letting a traveller pass through a country without staying is a kind of travel document.

clue.text: Bleak period's recalled with dark place underground

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, signals the word for dark is turned backwards

parts.note: dark means dim
to inter is to place a body underground, bury it

explanation.surface: A grim season is remembered alongside a gloomy cellar or cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns DIM into MID; 'place underground' is a verb, INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The depths of winter, around the solstice, are a proverbially bleak time of year.

clue.text: Barnet v remaining Dutch side, initially top

parts.note: Dutch is Cockney slang for a wife (my old Dutch); the one left after her husband dies is a widow

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of side is used

parts.note: a top is a peak or summit

explanation.surface: A football match report: Barnet against a Dutch side, with someone coming out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair); the v is the V-shaped point the hairline makes on the forehead, not 'versus'.
explanation.definitionFit: This hairline dips to a V-shaped point in the middle of the forehead, so it is a V of hair.

clue.text: Welsh team gets on by smashing London one

indicators.note: smashing, breaking into, signals letters forced inside the band's name

parts.note: Wham! was a pop duo from London
on means about, RE
by is the multiplication sign X, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A Welsh club makes progress by thrashing a London side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London one' looks like a football club but is the London pop group Wham!
explanation.definitionFit: The town's football club, Wrexham AFC, is a well-known Welsh team.

clue.text: I don't believe you and your unfunny jokes …

definitions.meaning: a scornful retort meaning that what was said is ridiculous
the sarcastic retort to someone whose jokes fall flat, which the ellipsis invites us to complete

explanation.surface: A dismissive reply to someone who is both unconvincing and not at all amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of disbelief, and also literally what one says to a person telling feeble jokes.

clue.text: New semi originally put people up for spells?

indicators.note: the letters of new semi are put in an original, fresh order

explanation.surface: A new semi-detached house is put up by builders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people up for spells?' means people who know about magic, not people standing for terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi or wizards of folklore were learned men skilled in sorcery and spells.

clue.text: Old spouse turning pictures over

parts.note: a former husband or wife is an ex

indicators.note: turning signals the word for pictures is read backwards

parts.note: pictures collectively are art

explanation.surface: A former partner flips through a photo album.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over and above the required amount is surplus or additional.

clue.text: College breaks up, oddly, halfway through Lent

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means those letters are read bottom to top
oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of breaks
halfway through takes the first half of the word Lent

explanation.surface: A college term break starts midway through the Lenten season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives BEK from 'breaks', and 'up' turns it into KEB.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: The wicked going to such extremes?

definitions.text: The wicked going to such extremes?

parts.words: The wicked going to such extremes?
parts.note: wicked here means fitted with wicks; candle stubs are what wicked things become at the very end

explanation.surface: A moralist wonders how far the evil will go.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubs left when tapers burn down are wicked objects at their extremities, burnt down to the last.

clue.text: Go from Barking in a westerly direction

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: barking, as in barking mad, means crazy, bats

explanation.surface: Directions for heading west out of Barking, a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, but here it means mad; 'in a westerly direction' turns BATS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go and having a stab both mean making an attempt.

clue.text: Wodehouse character abused this MP

indicators.note: abused, maltreated, signals the letters of this MP are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A comic novelist's creation has mistreated a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The monocled dandy with a silent P appears in several P. G. Wodehouse novels, such as Leave It to Psmith.

clue.text: Managed to occupy short leg and cover

short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a leg is a limb or member
managed, as in ran a business

explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' is a noun here, a thin covering layer, and 'leg' is a limb, not a stage of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin layer of tissue covering or lining an organ is a covering skin.

clue.text: Watches without alertness, perhaps, but does OK

definitions.meaning: dozing off throughout a show while watching it
approves something without debate, as a committee or Parliament may

explanation.surface: Someone dozes in front of the television yet still does all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, dozing for the whole of something; idiomatically, letting a motion pass on the nod.

clue.text: Figure skater's triple axel tackled upfront

indicators.note: upfront picks the front letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A figure skater attempts a difficult triple axel jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks part of 'figure skater' but is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistic, informally shortened, is a numerical figure.

clue.text: Prices on brand number to be all the same

indicators.note: the word for prices is placed after the other two

parts.note: a brand of product is a make
betting prices are odds

explanation.surface: A shopper notices prices of one brand are identical.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning it makes no difference, a matter of indifference either way.

clue.text: Above river in America, very strong bridge moves

explanation.definitionFit: At bridge, trumping with a higher trump than one already played is a card-play move.

clue.text: Saint converting your men with his

explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin name of St Jerome, translator of the Vulgate Bible.

clue.text: Length of thread but no hems of lace required

explanation.definitionFit: Needful is an old-fashioned adjective for necessary.

clue.text: Old instrument seen in wine bar

clue.text: Second-class no longer available, caps fare

clue.text: Bloomer which a rebel leader conceals

clue.text: Ken's called Deirdre at last

clue.text: Metal not commonly found in poison

an American, someone from across the Atlantic

clue.text: Vehicle the gendarmes would have come to seize?

definitions.text: Vehicle the gendarmes would have come to seize?

parts.words: Vehicle the gendarmes would have come to seize?
parts.note: seize is French for sixteen, and four times four comes to sixteen, so French police would reckon the sum equals seize

clue.text: In very high latitude, what forms large item going overhead

explanation.definitionFit: A tall conical hat of the fifteenth century was named for its church-spire shape, a large headpiece.

clue.text: What gardeners may do to be heard in the London area
